### 3 Chemical bonding - Multiple Choice: Easy

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q1 data-answer="B"}
### Question 1 · Coordinate bonding · 1.3 Choice Easy Q1
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q1</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q1](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q1.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q1"}
</details>

Phosphine, $\ce{PH3}$, reacts with a hydrogen ion to form $\ce{PH4+}$. Which type of bond is formed between P and H in this reaction?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Hydrogen bond</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Coordinate covalent bond</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Ionic bond</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Metallic bond</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The lone pair on phosphorus is donated to the electron-deficient $\ce{H+}$ ion.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q2 data-answer="D"}
### Question 2 · Bonding in iodine and silver · 1.3 Choice Easy Q2
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q2</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q2](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q2.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q2"}
</details>

Which forces act between neighbouring iodine molecules in solid iodine and between particles in solid silver?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Metallic bonds; covalent bonds</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Ionic bonds; metallic bonds</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Covalent bonds; covalent bonds</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>London dispersion forces; metallic bonds</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> $\ce{I2}$ molecules are held together by London forces; silver has a lattice of metal ions and delocalised electrons.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q3 data-answer="D"}
### Question 3 · More than one type of bonding · 1.3 Choice Easy Q3
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q3</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q3](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q3.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q3"}
</details>

Which solid contains more than one type of bonding?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Diamond</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Sodium chloride</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Iron</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Ice</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Ice contains covalent bonds within water molecules and hydrogen bonds between molecules.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q4 data-answer="B"}
### Question 4 · Shape of hydrazine · 1.3 Choice Easy Q4
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q4</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q4](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q4.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q4"}
</details>

What is the shape around each nitrogen atom in hydrazine, $\ce{N2H4}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Trigonal planar, $120^\circ$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Trigonal pyramidal, about $107^\circ$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Linear, $180^\circ$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Square planar, $90^\circ$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Each N has three bonding pairs and one lone pair. Lone-pair repulsion reduces the tetrahedral angle to about $107^\circ$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q5 data-answer="C"}
### Question 5 · Bond dipoles · 1.3 Choice Easy Q5
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q5</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q5](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q5.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q5"}
</details>

Which bond polarity assignment is not correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{C^{\delta+}-O^{\delta-}}$ in propanol</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{C^{\delta+}=O^{\delta-}}$ in propanal</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{C^{\delta+}-H^{\delta-}}$ in propane</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{C^{\delta+}-Cl^{\delta-}}$ in chloropropane</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Carbon is slightly more electronegative than hydrogen, so the C--H bond is treated as approximately non-polar rather than with H as $\delta-$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q6 data-answer="B"}
### Question 6 · Formation of ammonium · 1.3 Choice Easy Q6
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q6</summary>

</details>

Which statement correctly describes the formation of $\ce{NH4+}$ from $\ce{NH3}$ and $\ce{H+}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Hydrogen donates one electron to nitrogen.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Nitrogen donates its lone pair to hydrogen.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Four electrons are transferred from nitrogen to hydrogen.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>The hydrogen ion supplies a lone pair.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The N lone pair forms the fourth N--H coordinate bond.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q7 data-answer="C"}
### Question 7 · Shapes of boron compounds · 1.3 Choice Easy Q7
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q7</summary>

What are the shapes around boron in $\ce{BF3}$ and $\ce{BH4-}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Pyramidal; tetrahedral</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Pyramidal; square planar</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Trigonal planar; tetrahedral</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Trigonal planar; square planar</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q8 data-answer="A"}
### Question 8 · Electronegativity trend · 1.3 Choice Easy Q8
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q8</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q8](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q8.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q8"}
</details>

Which atom is most electronegative?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Cl</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Mg</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Br</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Na</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Electronegativity decreases down Group 17, so chlorine is more electronegative than bromine.</p></details>

### Question 9 · Ionic or covalent · 1.3 Choice Easy Q9
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q9</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Easy Q9](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-easy-q9.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Easy Q9"}
</details>

Which compound is not an ionic compound?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{CaCO3}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{CH3OH}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{NaOH}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{BaCl2}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Methanol is a molecular covalent substance. The other compounds contain ions, even though carbonate or hydroxide also contain covalent bonds internally.</p></details>

### Question 10 · Metallic bonding definition · 1.3 Choice Easy Q10
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q10</summary>

Which statement describes metallic bonding?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Attraction between oppositely charged ions</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Attraction between permanent molecular dipoles</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Attraction between shared pairs and two nuclei only</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Attraction between positive metal ions and delocalised electrons</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> This is the definition of metallic bonding.</p></details>

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-easy-q11 data-answer="B"}

<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Easy Q11</summary>

</details>

Which material contains only one main type of bonding in its solid structure?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Graphite</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Brass</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Ice</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Iodine crystals</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Brass is an alloy with metallic bonding. Graphite, ice and iodine have bonding within particles plus intermolecular attractions.</p></details>

### 3 Chemical bonding - Multiple Choice: Medium

### Question 15 · Equilibrium and molecular shape · 1.3 Choice Medium Q1
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Medium Q1</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Medium Q1](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-medium-q1.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Medium Q1"}
</details>

For $\ce{PCl5(g) <=> PCl3(g) + Cl2(g)}$, the percentage yield of $\ce{PCl3}$ increases from 13% at $160^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to 100% at $300^\circ\mathrm{C}$. What is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>The reaction is exothermic; $\ce{PCl3}$ is pyramidal.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>The reaction is exothermic; $\ce{PCl3}$ is trigonal planar.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>The reaction is endothermic; $\ce{PCl3}$ is pyramidal.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>The reaction is endothermic; $\ce{PCl3}$ is trigonal planar.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Higher temperature favours the endothermic forward reaction. $\ce{PCl3}$ has three bonds and one lone pair, giving a pyramidal shape.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-medium-q2 data-answer="C"}

Which feature is not present in a nitrogen molecule, $\ce{N2}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Two lone pairs in total</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Three shared electron pairs</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Three $\pi$ bonds</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>A bond angle of $180^\circ$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> A triple bond contains one $\sigma$ bond and two $\pi$ bonds.</p></details>

Which ion has three lone pairs around its central atom?

<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>

Which change of state involves overcoming only London dispersion forces?

What is the formula of the cyanate ion in ammonium cyanate?

Which pair of words does not correctly complete the statement: “The bond ___ between H and the halogen in HBr is ___ than in HI”?

How many $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds are in ethene, $\ce{C2H4}$?

Hydrogen bonding occurs between liquid methanal, $\ce{HCHO}$, and a second liquid $Y$. Which substance is most likely to be $Y$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{CH3CO2CH3}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{CH3OH}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{CH3COCH3}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{CH3CHO}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>

### Question 29 · Bond energy down a group · 1.3 Choice Hard Q2
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q2</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q2](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q2.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q2"}
</details>

Why does the rate of hydrolysis of $\ce{R-Cl}$, $\ce{R-Br}$ and $\ce{R-I}$ generally increase from chlorine to iodine?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>The first ionisation energy of the halogen increases.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>The silver halide solubility increases from chloride to iodide.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>The R--X bond energy decreases from R--Cl to R--I.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>The R--X bond polarity increases from R--Cl to R--I.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The larger iodine atom forms a longer, weaker R--I bond that breaks more readily.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q3 data-answer="A"}
### Question 30 · Electronegativity and covalent bonding · 1.3 Choice Hard Q3
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q3</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q3](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q3.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q3"}
</details>

Which atom is most likely to form a covalent bond with fluorine rather than an ionic bond, based on the smallest electronegativity difference?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>H, $\chi=2.20$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Cu, $\chi=1.95$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Mg, $\chi=1.30$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>K, $\chi=0.82$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Hydrogen has the closest electronegativity to fluorine among the options, so the H--F bond is covalent and strongly polar.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q4 data-answer="D"}
### Question 31 · Dipoles in molecules · 1.3 Choice Hard Q4
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q4</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q4](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q4.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q4"}
</details>

Which description of dipoles in $\ce{CHCl3}$ and $\ce{Br2}$ is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Induced only in both molecules</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Induced only in $\ce{CHCl3}$; induced and permanent in $\ce{Br2}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Induced and permanent in both</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Induced and permanent in $\ce{CHCl3}$; induced only in $\ce{Br2}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> $\ce{CHCl3}$ is polar, while symmetrical $\ce{Br2}$ is non-polar but still has temporary dipoles.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q5 data-answer="C"}
### Question 32 · Ionic lattice and bonding types · 1.3 Choice Hard Q5
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q5</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q5](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q5.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q5"}
</details>

Hydroxyapatite contains calcium, hydroxide and phosphate ions. Which statement is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>It contains only metallic bonding.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Strontium forms covalent bonds with phosphate ions.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Strontium ions are similar enough in size to replace calcium ions in the lattice.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Phosphate ions are held together by metallic bonding.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Similar-sized ions can occupy similar lattice sites; the bonding between calcium/strontium ions and anions is ionic.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q6 data-answer="A"}
### Question 33 · Conductivity and lattice structure · 1.3 Choice Hard Q6
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q6</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q6](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q6.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q6"}
</details>

Which substance is expected to have a high melting point and conduct electricity when molten but not when solid?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>A giant ionic compound</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>A simple molecular compound</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>A noble gas</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>A molecular non-polar liquid</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Strong ionic attractions give a high melting point; mobile ions in the molten state carry charge.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q7 data-answer="D"}
### Question 34 · Expanded electron-pair arrangement · 1.3 Choice Hard Q7
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q7</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q7](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q7.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q7"}
</details>

What is the shape of $\ce{PF6-}$?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Tetrahedral</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Trigonal pyramidal</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Trigonal bipyramidal</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Octahedral</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Six bonding pairs around phosphorus repel to an octahedral arrangement.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q8 data-answer="B"}
### Question 35 · Hydrogenation of an alkene · 1.3 Choice Hard Q8
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q8</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q8](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q8.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q8"}
</details>

Which feature disappears when $\ce{C2H4}$ is converted to $\ce{C2H6}$ by hydrogenation?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>The C--C $\sigma$ bond</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>The C--C $\pi$ bond</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>All C--H $\sigma$ bonds</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>All electron pairs on carbon</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Hydrogen adds across the double bond, converting the $\pi$ component into two new C--H bonds.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #bonding-choice-hard-q9 data-answer="B"}
### Question 36 · Overall dipole and symmetry · 1.3 Choice Hard Q9
<details class="source-preview"><summary>Original question page · 1.3 Choice Hard Q9</summary>
![Original question page for 1.3 Choice Hard Q9](../assets/questions/original-source/1-3-choice-hard-q9.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Original question page 1.3 Choice Hard Q9"}
</details>

Which molecule has the largest overall dipole?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{CCl4}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{CH2Cl2}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{BF3}$</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{CO2}$</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The tetrahedral $\ce{CH2Cl2}$ molecule is not symmetrical enough for its bond dipoles to cancel.</p></details>
:::
